data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# Resources
# Slurm: -n 16, -N 1
flux submit --batch \
  -N 1 \
  -n 16 \
  --time-limit=8h \
  --setattr=system.job.shell=/bin/bash \
  --setattr=system.stdout.path=logs/dsmc_job_%j.out \
  --setattr=system.stderr.path=logs/dsmc_job_%j.err \
  --setattr=system.stdout.mode=append \
  --setattr=system.stderr.mode=append \
  --env=OMP_PROC_BIND=spread \
  --env=OMP_PLACES=threads \
  --env=JULIA_NUM_THREADS=16 \
  bash -lc '

module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

echo "running...."

julia RunCells.jl -l 0.001 -L 0.02
'

# Omitted Slurm option: -p shared (partition)
# Flux uses queues/partitions only if configured by the site; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may land on a different set of nodes/resources than intended (or be rejected if policy requires a specific queue).

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu 512
# Flux has no universally portable per-CPU memory request in the batch CLI without site-specific configuration.
# Performance implication: the job could be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or reduced performance due to memory pressure.

# Note: Slurm variable $SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE is not available under Flux.
# Set JULIA_NUM_THREADS explicitly above to match -n 16.

reasons: Output/error file patterns use Slurm's %j token (logs/dsmc_job_%j.out / .err). Flux does not expand %j in these attributes; this can cause all jobs to write to the same literal filename and lead to output interleaving/corruption.

The script requests 16 tasks (-n 16) but does not specify per-task CPU needs (e.g., --cores-per-task/--cpus-per-task equivalent). If the intent was 16 cores on one node for a single Julia process with threads, resources may be misrequested (16 separate tasks rather than 1 task with 16 cores), impacting scheduling and performance.
issues: This is a submission wrapper (calls `flux submit --batch ...`) rather than a Flux batch script that Flux executes directly (i.e., a script with `#flux:` directives). It will work when run in a Flux instance, but it's a different execution model than a native batch script.
The `module` command requires the environment-modules init in non-interactive shells; `bash -lc` helps, but it still depends on site configuration.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -n 16 # Number of cores requested
#SBATCH -N 1 # Ensure that all cores are on one machine
#SBATCH -t 0-08:00 # Runtime in minutes
#SBATCH -p shared # Partition to submit to
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu 512 # Memory per cpu in MB (see also ?mem-per-cpu)
#SBATCH --open-mode=append
#SBATCH -o logs/dsmc_job_%j.out # Standard out goes to this file
#SBATCH -e logs/dsmc_job_%j.err # Standard err goes to this filehostname

module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=threads
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE

echo "running...."

julia RunCells.jl -l 0.001 -L 0.02
